our_interpretation: The plain reading predicts a continuing industry dependence on substantial human work to identify and correct new failures, with the routine corrective process largely hidden from users.
Band-aids can include changes to training, model weights, prompts, retrieval, safeguards, or other system components.

The disclosure allegation concerns the general visibility of routine corrective work. One published fix does not by itself refute it; isolated disclosures and promises of transparency must be distinguished from comprehensive practice.
Forever and endlessly supply no deadline. Repeated failures during a finite period cannot establish permanent dependence.
Massive numbers means substantial human labor devoted to this corrective process. The speaker supplies neither a headcount threshold nor a denominator.
criteria.support_condition: Longitudinal audits show continued substantial human correction of newly encountered failures and limited disclosure of routine interventions across representative companies. Such evidence supports the observed pattern but cannot conclusively establish that it continues forever.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Independently verified, sustained changes across representative deployed systems demonstrate that the industry has escaped dependence on recurring human correction of new failures. Comprehensive disclosure records could separately contradict the opacity component; isolated announcements cannot settle the compound forecast.
